name: Hurika

related.relation: the eastern ledge and the nest

facts.text: Hurika is a level-85 creature with 100,000 health, Torst's mate on the high ledge; the original patrol flight is switched off.
A gust from her wings sends a random attacker flying into the air.
A June 2003 Allakhazam comment asks if anyone has ever killed 'this bird'; a European raid of about 60 answered that they did, by bolt-pulling her down.

Hurika has no spells: 100,000 health, 40% melee / 70% magic resists, CC-immune, reach 350. Every 15-20 s she picks a random real player and announces that a gust of wind sends them flying, but the throw itself is OFF in Living Server (EpicEncounterMechanics.AllowDisplacement), and so is her aerial patrol (AllowGlacierGriffonPatrol); she keeps her perch.
Hrafn's spear through her wing and the icelord she once threw off the ledge are Living Server lore; Hrafn is the wind-rider of four attempts in the existing roost lore.

story:
Hurika is the hen of the griffon roost on Tuscaran's eastern ledge and the larger of the pair, a griffon icewing so old the iarn dwarves say their grandmothers' grandmothers saw her fly. Her feathers are white as frost and her quills are prized by the fletchers of Midgard beyond anything, though they will not say what they make of them. She is guarding a nest, and she has no other thought.

Where Torst freezes the air, she moved it. For a century one beat of her wings could put a man in the sky with nothing under him, and the hrimthursa say she once threw an icelord of the old houses clean off the ledge for coming too close to her chicks; the icelords say nothing about it at all. The wind-riders of the Vind Ryttaren who tried for her nest took to keeping their griffons low and their saddles tied, and still she sent them tumbling.

Then Hrafn came. On his fourth and last attempt on the roost the wind-rider put a spear through her wing as she rose over the nest, and the lift went out of it. She can beat her wings still and raise a gale over the ledge that howls through the eastern halls of the citadel, and the giants still hear it and say Hurika is throwing again. But nothing leaves the ground. She has not flown since, and Torst will not fly without her. The two of them keep the ledge with the nest between them, and Hrafn, who lived, does not fly either. Her quills still come down the crater road with the companies, and the fletchers of Midgard still pay more for them than for anything else off the glacier; the wind-riders say an arrow fletched with one flies against the wind, which the fletchers neither confirm nor deny.

chapters.title: The Hen of the Roost
chapters.text:
Hurika is older than Torst, the iarn dwarves say, and larger, and she has had more than one mate on the eastern ledge in the time the slates of Faraheim have been watching her. The dwarves' grandmothers' grandmothers saw her fly. Her feathers are white as frost, whiter than his, and when she spreads her wings over the nest the ledge goes into shadow from end to end.

She is guarding a nest, and the wind-riders who have watched her longest say she has no other thought. The griffon chicks of the glacier are small and loud and grey, and they spend their first winters on the high ledge learning to fly into the wind their mother makes for them, beating their stubby wings against it and falling over and getting up. The giants of the citadel, who do not often say anything kind about anything, say the chicks are the only things on the glacier that laugh.

Her quills are prized by the fletchers of Midgard beyond anything else that comes off the glacier. The fletchers will not say what they make of them, and the companies who bring them home are paid more than they expect, and not told why. The wind-riders say an arrow fletched with Hurika's quill flies against the wind. The fletchers say nothing.

The hen does not care about the quills. She cares about the nest. Everything else on the eastern ledge, the giants say, the cold and the eddies and her mate, is only the wall round it.

chapters.title: The Gale
chapters.text:
Where Torst freezes the air, Hurika moved it. For as long as the giants have watched the ledge, one beat of her wings could put a man in the sky with nothing under him: up, tumbling, and then down, on the ice of the ledge or past the edge of it. The wind-riders of the Vind Ryttaren knew that before they knew anything else about the eastern roost, and they had it from the bodies of their first riders on the crater floor.

The hrimthursa have a story about it that the icelords will not discuss. They say that in the Council's thirtieth winter a young icelord of the old houses climbed to the eastern ledge to look at the chicks, out of curiosity, and went too close to the nest, and the hen beat her wings once, and the icelord went off the ledge and down the whole eastern face of the glacier, and walked home with both arms broken. The icelords say nothing about it at all, which the giants take as proof.

The wind-riders who kept trying for her nest took to flying low, under the gale, and to tie themselves into their saddles, and still she sent them tumbling. Asmund, who made seven attempts on the roost, said Hurika threw him four times and he never once saw her wings move; he only felt the ledge go away. He said the cock was the one you watched and the hen was the one that killed you.

For a century nobody came near the nest who was not thrown away from it. Then Hrafn came.

chapters.title: Hrafn's Spear
chapters.text:
Hrafn of the Vind Ryttaren made four attempts on the roost, and on the last he did not try for a chick. The wind-riders say he had decided, after the third, that nobody would take a chick of the eastern ledge while the hen could fly, and that he went up the fourth time to stop her flying.

He came in low, under the gale, as the riders had taken to doing, on the best griffon of the cliffs, with a long spear across his saddle. Hurika rose over the nest to throw him, and he did not turn away from her. He flew straight up into the wind of her wings and put the spear through the joint of the left one as she beat it, and the gale took him and his griffon and threw them off the ledge, and his griffon died on the crater floor and Hrafn did not.

The lift went out of her wing. She could beat it still. She can still raise a gale over the ledge that howls through the eastern halls of the citadel, so loud that the giants hear it and say to each other that Hurika is throwing again. But nothing she beats her wings at leaves the ground any more. The wind goes over them and round them and the ledge stays under their feet. The companies of Midgard who have come up to the roost since say the gale is the most frightening thing they have ever stood in that did nothing.

She has not flown since that season. The wind-riders say the spear-head is still in the joint of her wing, and that she will not let Torst near it.

chapters.title: The Nest Between Them
chapters.text:
Hrafn lived. He never flew again, the wind-riders say, though nothing was broken in him that the menders of the cliffs could see; he goes up onto the cliffs at dawn and looks east, and comes down. He has never said whether he is sorry. The wind-riders do not ask him.

The two griffons keep the ledge now with the nest between them. Torst will not fly the circuit without her, and so neither of them leaves the roost, and the giants of the citadel, who used to watch the sky for them at dawn and dusk, have stopped looking up. The wind-riders have not made an attempt on the roost in years. Some of them say it is because the nest is never alone now. Asmund said it was because of what Hrafn had done, and that none of them wanted to be the next one to do it.

The chicks still take their first flights on the ledge, into the wind their mother makes for them, and the cast-out sculptors say that is the saddest thing on the glacier: a mother who cannot fly teaching her young into a gale that cannot lift anything. The chicks fly anyway. They leave the ledge in their second or third spring, and the hen watches them go.

When she falls, the companies say, the gale stops all at once, and the chicks in the nest go quiet, and the only sound on the eastern ledge is Torst. The wind-riders say he does not cry out. He goes to the edge and spreads his wings and looks back at the nest, and folds them again, as he does every dawn.

legend: Hurika is a plain melee griffon now: 100,000 health, 40% melee and 70% magic resists, CC-immune, long reach, and no spells. The old guides all say she throws people into the air or off the ledge. Not here: that's switched off. You'll still see 'a powerful gust sends X flying' every 15 to 20 seconds, but nobody moves, so ignore it. Neither griffon patrols any more either, so forget the bolt-pull: fight them on their perches. She sits next to Torst and they usually come together, so the real work is Torst's eddies and his root switching onto you. Kill whichever suits your raid. Her quills and the shadowed eye are the drops, and fletchers pay well.

loremasterTopic.text: The hen of the griffon roost, older than her mate [Torst]. For a century one beat of her wings threw anything near the nest off the ledge. Then the wind-rider Hrafn flew into her wind and put a spear through her wing, and the lift went out of it. Her gale still howls over the ledge, but nothing leaves the ground. Neither griffon flies now.

bookPage: From the sayings of Asmund of the Vind Ryttaren, as the wind-riders of the cliffs repeat them. The cock is the one you watch. The hen is the one that kills you. I went up seven times and she threw me four, and I never once saw her wings move; I only felt the ledge go away. Hrafn went up four times and on the fourth he flew into her wind instead of away from it. He took the sky from her. I do not know whether that was brave. I know that I am glad I did not do it, and that he does not fly any more, and neither does she.
